I'll solve this problem from scratch by calculating 48^14 and counting the 1 bits in its binary representation.
<function_calls>
<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="command">cd /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-RSI/ebd00391-ba98-5b98-9125-83abd1dce979/scratchpad && python3 << 'EOF'
# Calculate 48^14
n = 48 ** 14

# Get binary representation
binary_rep = bin(n)  # Returns string like '0b...'

# Count the number of 1's in the binary representation
count_ones = binary_rep.count('1')

print(f"48^14 = {n}")
print(f"Binary representation: {binary_rep}")
print(f"Number of 1 bits: {count_ones}")

EOF
</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>
